questionText: What is the embedded server in Spring Boot and why is it significant?

target.learningOutcome: The learner can define an embedded server, explain its lifecycle and deployment value, switch the servlet-server dependency, and state its operational limits.
outOfScope: Claiming embedded packaging is cloud-native by itself

claims.statement: A Boot servlet application uses a ServletWebServerApplicationContext and ServletWebServerFactory to start the embedded server during context initialization.
The servlet web starter uses Tomcat by default, supported server starters can replace it, and Boot also supports traditional WAR deployment.

examples.title: Boot application launcher with server properties and deployment sketch

validation.expected: The example labels the web-starter condition and does not present embedded packaging as an operational guarantee

visuals.title: Executable JAR and external WAR deployment models

notes: Resource limits, TLS, graceful shutdown, health checks, and scaling remain explicit operational responsibilities.

review.notes: Embedded servlet server and traditional deployment claims were checked against Spring Boot 3.3.1 documentation; final fixture and editorial review remain open.
